ideas.title: A step‑by‑step 'What to expect on your first Wednesday' guide to help hesitant adults decide to try the taster
ideas.description: A short, vividly practical piece that walks a hesitant adult through the actual evening: who is invited, no auditions/no need to read music, the shared warm‑up with an option to listen, the 19:00 start and quiet entry until 19:20, and the free first taster with normal contribution from visit two — written to reduce uncertainty and lower the barrier to attend.
ideas.audience: Adults who are unsure about singing in a group and are weighing whether to attend a one‑off taster
ideas.rationale: The source frames the notice to help a hesitant newcomer 'picture the evening' and the choir's own informal feedback shows 'welcome' was the dominant reason people said they'd return; the committee also retained a later entry window — together these facts make a practical, expectation‑setting feature likely to address the main barrier signalled in the source.
ideas.evidence: Source provides the taster details (who's invited, practical arrangements and free first visit), the short rehearsal feedback showing welcome as the top return reason, and the committee decision to keep a later entry window — while also noting there has been no formal survey of confidence or a fixed‑start comparison.

ideas.title: Brief internal report for the choir committee summarising rehearsal feedback and the decision to keep the later‑entry window
ideas.description: A concise two‑panel memo: (1) document the October micro‑survey counts (12 answered; 8 cited welcome, 3 songs, 1 both; two missed due to late trains), (2) note the committee decision to retain later entry through December and that minutes record the decision without explaining why, (3) flag gaps in evidence (no confidence survey, no fixed‑start comparison).
ideas.audience: Choir committee and volunteer organisers who make access and scheduling decisions
ideas.rationale: The rehearsal responses and the recorded committee decision are present in the source; packaging those facts and the recorded evidence gaps will support clearer governance and any future, justified operational choices.
ideas.evidence: The source lists the micro‑survey counts and reasons given by members, records the committee decision to keep the later entry window, and explicitly states there has been no survey comparing confidence or fixed‑start rehearsals.

grounding.claim: The feature should explicitly aim to help hesitant newcomers picture a first evening so they can decide whether to come.
grounding.sourceEvidence: The notice is intended to help a hesitant newcomer picture the evening and decide whether to come.
grounding.inference: The sentence explicitly states the notice's purpose; a title framing the piece as a 'what to expect' guide follows directly from that stated intent.
grounding.constraints: This supports framing the piece for hesitant newcomers for this specific taster; it does not prove that this framing will increase attendance or apply beyond this event.

grounding.claim: The practical details to include are: invited adults unsure about group singing, no auditions/no music‑reading requirement, first twenty minutes shared warm‑up with option to listen, 19:00 start with quiet entry until 19:20, and a free first taster with normal contribution from the second visit.
grounding.sourceEvidence: Moorfield community choir is inviting adults who are unsure about singing in a group to a Wednesday taster on 25 November. There are no auditions and no requirement to read music. The first twenty minutes are a shared warm-up; newcomers may listen before joining in. The session begins at 19:00, but someone arriving from work may enter quietly until 19:20. A first taster is free; the ordinary weekly contribution applies from the second visit.
grounding.inference: Each clause enumerates a practical condition the notice already sets out; including those same specifics in a guide directly maps to the source's content and purpose.
grounding.constraints: These details are taken from the notice as written for this event; they may change for other sessions or future dates and do not indicate effectiveness in reducing hesitation.

grounding.claim: The intended audience is adults who are unsure about singing in a group.
grounding.sourceEvidence: Moorfield community choir is inviting adults who are unsure about singing in a group to a Wednesday taster on 25 November.
grounding.inference: The invitation sentence names the population the taster targets; therefore the recommended audience for the editorial piece should match that same group.
grounding.constraints: The quote identifies the target for this taster only; it does not quantify this population or their specific motivations beyond being 'unsure'.

grounding.claim: Focusing the piece on lowering arrival/startup friction is justified because informal feedback emphasised the 'welcome' as the main return reason and the choir chose to retain a later entry window.
grounding.sourceEvidence: After the October rehearsal, twelve of the nineteen people present answered a short question about returning. Eight mentioned the welcome, three mentioned the songs, and one mentioned both. Two people who had missed the previous rehearsal said late trains had played a part. The choir agreed at its monthly meeting to keep the later entry window through December.
grounding.inference: The micro‑survey counts show 'welcome' was the most-cited reason for returning; the committee's recorded operational choice to keep a later entry window is an action consistent with reducing arrival friction — together these facts support an editorial angle emphasising welcome and arrival practicalities.
grounding.constraints: The source gives counts from a short, informal question and a recorded decision without explaining committee motives; it does not establish causal effects (e.g., that later entry increases attendance) nor report a representative survey.

grounding.claim: The source combines the taster notice, short rehearsal feedback with counts, the committee's recorded decision, and an explicit statement that no formal pre/post confidence survey or fixed‑start comparison exists.
grounding.sourceEvidence: After the October rehearsal, twelve of the nineteen people present answered a short question about returning. Eight mentioned the welcome, three mentioned the songs, and one mentioned both. Two people who had missed the previous rehearsal said late trains had played a part. The choir agreed at its monthly meeting to keep the later entry window through December. The minutes record the decision without an account of why it was chosen. There has been no survey of confidence before and after singing and no comparison with a fixed-start rehearsal.
grounding.inference: This contiguous block contains the rehearsal feedback (counts and reasons), the committee decision and its unreported rationale, and the explicit data gap; these constitute the primary evidence items that anchor the editorial opportunity and its limits.
grounding.constraints: The evidence is limited to what the source reports: an informal short question answered by a subset of attendees, recorded minutes lacking rationale, and an absence of formal surveys — it does not provide broader longitudinal data or tested interventions.
